Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:172521
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40128 of 2024

Applicant :- Nanku @ Pawan Kumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Manvendra Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Manvendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
56 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Jafarganj, District Fatehpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is brother in law (devar) of the deceased and on the basis of false allegations of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter alongwith other family members including husband of the deceased.
4.

He further submitted that actually, after marriage, deceased started living separately with her husband and this fact is evident from the statement of the informant and other prosecution witnesses recorded during investigation which have been annexed at page 56 onwards of the paper book.

sentences.text: 5. He further submitted that as applicant resided separately from the deceased and therefore, he was not having any concern with the family affairs of the deceased and it appears some dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter her husband beaten her and thereafter she consumed some poisonous substance.

6. He further submitted that during the post mortem of the deceased, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved and viscera report is now on record which suggests that due to consumption of organo chloro insecticide, deceased died.

7. He further submitted that only being younger brother of the husband of deceased, it appears,
informant implicated the applicant alongwith his other family members including husband of the deceased.
8. He further submitted that there is no specific allegation against the applicant and applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 7.8.2024.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that applicant is brother in law (devar) of the deceased and even as per prosecution witnesses, he resided separately alongwith the in-laws of the deceased.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, bhabhi of the applicant died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is brother in law of the deceased i.e. devar and there is no specific allegation against him.

12. Further, from the statement of prosecution witnesses recorded during investigation which have been annexed alongwith the instant bail application, it reflects that deceased resided separately alongwith her husband.

Further, however, autopsy report suggests, deceased sustained number of contusions but her cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved and viscera report shows deceased died due to consumption of insecticide.

Therefore, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is not having any concern with the family affairs of the deceased and it reflects that some dispute arose between husband and wife and thereafter husband caused injury to her and therefore, she consumed some poisonous substance, cannot be ruled out, at this stage.
13.
Further, applicant is having no previous criminal history and in the present matter, he is in jail since 7.8.2024 i.e. for last almost three months.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant-Nanku @ Pawan Kumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
